title: AppShell navigation contract

component.note: Say AppShell in prose. In code import what the installed SDK exports: today that is ProShell (there is no AppShell export). If AppShell is added, ProShell stays as a temporary alias.

rules.title: AppShell owns one primary app navigation
rules.rule: An app has exactly one primary navigation and the shell renders it.
rules.why: A second navbar defeats the shell's responsive menu and gives assistive technology two competing landmarks.

rules.title: Every primary destination is in nav or renderNav
rules.rule: Put every primary destination in the `nav` prop, or in a `renderNav` replacement that renders the same destinations.
rules.why: A shell that renders `<ProShell nav={NAV}>` with an empty or landing-only NAV passes a superficial check and gives the user no navigation.

rules.title: Do not render a second primary navbar in shell content
rules.rule: Content area headers, sidebars and tab bars must not duplicate the primary destinations. `hideTopbar` also hides the navigation; a custom `renderTopbar` must place `ctx.nav` itself.
rules.why: Duplicated primary navigation is the failure this contract exists to prevent.

rules.title: Use onNavigate for SPA apps
rules.rule: A router-driven app passes its router's navigate function as `onNavigate`. Without it nav items are ordinary links that reload the document.
rules.why: A reload throws away client state and breaks back/forward expectations.

rules.title: Preserve tenant and workspace scope in links
rules.rule: Keep the scope in the path (for example `/w/acme/cases`). The shell matches a nav item's `href` against `location.pathname` only, so an `href` carrying a query string is never marked current.
rules.why: A link that drops the workspace silently shows the wrong tenant's data; a query-scoped href loses `aria-current`.

rules.title: Test the menu at a mobile viewport
rules.rule: Run a browser test against the real shell at 375px: a labelled Menu button, every destination listed, Escape and outside click close it, `aria-current` follows selection, no document reload, one navigation landmark.
rules.why: Tests that mock the shell as a plain div never see the hamburger, so a broken menu passes them.

rules.title: Know which navigation is outside this rule
rules.rule: Tabs inside one screen, breadcrumbs, a local admin sub-navigation, footer links, in-content links and the profile menu are not primary navigation and may exist beside it.
rules.why: The rule is about the app's primary destinations, not every link on the page.

checklist: The app renders the shell once and passes its destinations as `nav` or `renderNav`.
`nav` lists every primary destination, not only the landing route.
No other component renders the app's primary destinations.
Links keep tenant or workspace scope in the path.
Role-based items are hidden for presentation only; the server enforces access.
A mobile (375px) browser test runs against the real shell and checks the menu.
